transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Tom, have you got a minute? I need to finalise the plans for the away day, and I'd like your opinion.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Sure. What's the situation?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: We have forty staff and a budget of two thousand pounds. The date is the fourteenth of June. My first thought was to go to the coast, but the coach would cost nearly four hundred pounds, so I'm not sure.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: What about somewhere closer? The old mill by the river has a conference room we could hire for a day.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I looked into that. It's cheap, only three hundred and fifty, but the room holds just thirty people, so it's too small.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Hmm. What about the sports centre next to the office? We wouldn't need transport, and they have a large hall and a café.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I hadn't thought of that. And we could organise team sports in the afternoon.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Yes, but not everyone enjoys sport. Last year, several people said they felt uncomfortable with the football match.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: True. We could offer a choice: football for some, a quiz or a treasure hunt for others.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That sounds fair. What about the morning?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I'd like a workshop on communication between departments. That was the most frequent complaint in the staff survey.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Do you have a trainer in mind?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes, Dr Miller from the business school. She's very good, but her fee is eight hundred pounds.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That's a lot of the budget. Could one of our own managers lead it instead?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I considered that, but people tend to listen more carefully to someone from outside. I think it's worth paying.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: All right. And lunch?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: The sports centre café can provide sandwiches and salads for twelve pounds a head. That's four hundred and eighty pounds.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: So the hall hire, trainer and lunch come to quite a lot. Do we know the price of the hall?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Five hundred pounds for the full day. So the total is one thousand seven hundred and eighty. That leaves two hundred and twenty for activities.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That's enough for prizes and equipment. One more thing: will senior management attend?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: The director said she'd come for the morning, but she has a meeting after lunch.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Fine. Shall I send the invitation?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes, please, by Friday. And ask people to tell us about dietary requirements.
